    What is Last.FM?
    
      Last.fm is a music tracking service that logs—or "scrobbles"—every song you play across platforms into a personalized listening history. Unlike traditional music billboards that measure commercial sales, streaming promotions, and radio airplay driven by passive listeners, Last.fm reflects the habits of passionate, dedicated music enthusiasts. Because listeners intentionally track their libraries and dive deep into full artist catalogs over years, Last.fm data highlights enduring favorites and diverse, underground tastes rather than fleeting viral hits.

      Unlike algorithmic platforms with rigid genre taxonomies, Last.fm’s catalog is entirely community-built. Through collaborative "folksonomy," millions of listeners tag, correct, and catalogue tracks organically—capturing everything from broad global movements like rock and electronic to hyper-niche microgenres and local basement scenes. With user-curated album notes, artist wikis, and discography archives spanning decades, Last.fm serves as one of the most extensive, crowd-powered music databases in existence.
